body:
Independent fresh-context review of the exact head `b59b141e379c4c0cb73a1e0ab2c5242fef33d9cd`, by two models of different families, each in a fresh read-only context that did not author the change.

**Verdict: APPROVE — no P0 findings, no P1 findings.**

What the review verified:

- The bound is enforced at three independent layers, and a test fails when any one of them is removed: the server in front of the gateway refuses a body over the limit before the application sees it, the application refuses a body whose declared length is over the limit before it reads it, and the body is read from the raw input with a limit of its own.
- The limit of the request is the same for a declared length, an undeclared length and a chunked request, and a body of exactly the limit is accepted while one byte more is refused.
- A body over the limit is refused in the OpenAI error shape (`413`, `request_too_large`), and a body a megabyte over the limit is refused by the server in front with a plain-text `413`, because it cannot answer with that shape.
- The check of an inline image never refuses a payload that would have fitted: the bound on the encoded text is a safe over-approximation, and the exact size is checked after the decode.
- Nothing reads the body a second time, and no other code path reads it outside the two routes that go through the bounded read.

The reviews drove two rounds of fixes, each with a regression test that fails against the pre-change code: a request whose length was not declared was read to its end, so the excess went unnoticed and the request was answered from the truncated text; and the budget of a request was smaller than the inline images the per-image limit allows together, so a request the gateway had served before was refused.

The README now says what a request at the budget costs in memory, and that three images of the image limit do not fit.

The `CI` and `dco` checks are green on this head.
